answer: Every epoch, at local solar zenith, a member taps a serialized onyx puck in a registered room and records six seconds of decay; the ledger keeps that room's modal frequencies and reverberation time. Zenith timing keeps temperature comparable, while a sparse wooden trellis left in one corner scatters highs in a pattern unique to that geometry. Near-identical curves mean one room claims two seats, so both bonds are slashed. A sybil farmer must rent a thousand rooms, mount a thousand onyx pucks, and have someone clap in each at noon, paying real rent and deposits, not minting free keys.
